body:
Hey @apollo13 — Thanks for the review. I've made various adjustments/simplifications based on your comments. 

* Adjusted the SECRET_KEY(S) normalisation in `Settings.__init__()`. (Happy for you to suggest a different approach there...) 
* Check `all()` keys in `LazySettings.__getattr__()`
* Removed the `constant_time_any()`
* Moved `PasswordResetTokenGenerator` directly to `secrets` (It's not public API but I will add release note for this last as a breaking change.)

Can I get you to take another look? 

I will make the docs adjustments in the meantime. 

Thanks 👍

OK, just an update, we're going to target this for 4.0. It makes sense at the high-level but:

* As nice as it would be, it's too close to the feature freeze — It's too hot™: it's a sensitive area and it needs a slower review. 
* There are a whole load of overlapping changes in 3.2 (including #12553 which is still to come in) such that ^^^ is amplified. 
* We're dropping all pre-Django 3.1 token support in 4.0, which means a whole another batch of similarly overlapping changes. 
* Writing the docs, it doesn't make sense without ultimately deprecating the scalar SECRET_KEY.
* and so on... 

Bumping to 4.0 takes the pressure off of getting all of that right (in too tight a time frame). We've lasted 15 years without key rotation. 8 more months will be fine.

> Can I get you to take another look?

Sure, given that we are pushing this out of 3.2, I'll take a little bit more time with it. Remind me if I forget :)
@carltongibson I lost track of that, what is the current status here? Really like to have that in 4.0

Hey @apollo13 it's on my long list for 4.0. 

If you wanted to pick it up to play with, that would be great.

Otherwise I'll be asking for your input anyhow. 😀

Hey @apollo13 — I've updated this, sketched out the docs adjustments, and addressed previous comments. Can I get you to take a look again? 

I'm looking at @kezabelle's comments now. (Handle `UserSettingsHolder`, and tighten up the system checks.) 

We're essentially using `SECRET_KEYS[0]` internally. So the bit I'm 😬 about is the mapping back to `SECRET_KEY`, that I think we need, since everything out there is using it. (…)

Hi @kezabelle, @ngnpope, @apollo13 — thanks for taking an interest in this one! (Important to get it right.)

@ngnpope and @apollo13 — I accept your points above — +1 — I'll work those in. 

I was thinking about @kezabelle's review comments above… 

Specifically, the thing that's been bothering me is trying to keep the values of `SECRET_KEY` and `SECRET_KEYS` in sync. It's two sources of truth, and that's (pretty much) always an error. 

Thinking about this for `UserSettingsHolder`, I thought the best way would be if `SECRET_KEY` became a property, aliasing to the (now) one source of truth. 

I added that in 2f1d3a397e621a1a0f82a91bbd00e7c950599dc6. Can I ask you to take a look? What do you think? Everything passes, and it removed the duplicate `Normalize SECRET_KEY(S)` kludges. 

If we think that's neater I can clean up, document `SECRET_KEYS` as preferred,  and that `SECRET_KEYS[1:]` incur a penalty (so shouldn't hang around), adjusting the signing checks as suggested, and so on.  

Thanks!

Hi all — thanks again for the input here! 

* I've pulled in @apollo13's suggestion ref breaking from the comparison loops. 
* Adjusted settings docs to point strongly towards the new SECRET_KEYS, given that SECRET_KEY is now a (mere) proxy, that we **might** remove some day. 

I've asked @felixxm to give it his fully-considered look next week, but any other comments very much appreciated. Are we going to do this? Are we happy with the general approach? Any other comments?

* I will go over the checks wording and other occurrences of `SECRET_KEY` this afternoon. 
* I'll leave the multiple commits for the moment to leave the context for review.

OK, I've gone through all the docs and tests to use `SECRET_KEYS` (unless specifically testing `SECRET_KEY`). 

The one thing on my list is to looks at the usages in the checks (and checks.txt) which I'll do next week. 

Then it's _Any other comments_ and getting it past @felixxm 😄. 

I think it's a nice feature, but if there are objections, please do raise 'em now. 😝

Hey @felixxm. I've squashed this and rebased. 

* Below is the diff moving to the property. The original way was trying to sync the two settings values, but I think the property comes out much cleaner. (There's still the duplication with `UserSettingsHolder` which could be reduced.) Thoughts welcome! 
* Current docs lean to _"Use `SECRET_KEYS`!"_ but `SECRET_KEY` could be fine for most folks, so we could adjust the messaging there to "Use `SECRET_KEYS` if you need key rotation."
* What extra tests do you want? 😄 


<details>
<summary>diff moving to property, rather than trying to keep values in-sync</summary>

```diff

From 44947f9c44e28dc4f20cea6546584e87ab016740 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Carlton Gibson <carlton.gibson@noumenal.es>
Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2021 10:49:19 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] Made SECRET_KEY a property on Settings/UserSettingsHolder.

---
 django/conf/__init__.py         | 46 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++-------
 django/test/utils.py            |  8 ------
 tests/auth_tests/test_tokens.py |  2 +-
 3 files changed, 37 insertions(+), 19 deletions(-)

diff --git a/django/conf/__init__.py b/django/conf/__init__.py
index dfd7235477..279c359c4e 100644
--- a/django/conf/__init__.py
+++ b/django/conf/__init__.py
@@ -186,6 +186,9 @@ class Settings:
         self.SETTINGS_MODULE = settings_module
 
         mod = importlib.import_module(self.SETTINGS_MODULE)
+        if hasattr(mod, 'SECRET_KEY') and hasattr(mod, 'SECRET_KEYS'):
+            if mod.SECRET_KEY and mod.SECRET_KEYS:
+                raise ImproperlyConfigured('Only one of SECRET_KEY and SECRET_KEYS can be specified, not both.')
 
         tuple_settings = (
             'ALLOWED_HOSTS',
@@ -202,6 +205,8 @@ class Settings:
                         not isinstance(setting_value, (list, tuple))):
                     raise ImproperlyConfigured("The %s setting must be a list or a tuple." % setting)
                 setattr(self, setting, setting_value)
+                if setting == 'SECRET_KEY':
+                    setting = 'SECRET_KEYS'
                 self._explicit_settings.add(setting)
 
         if self.USE_TZ is False and not self.is_overridden('USE_TZ'):
@@ -212,16 +217,6 @@ class Settings:
                 category=RemovedInDjango50Warning,
             )
 
-        # Normalize SECRET_KEY/SECRET_KEYS when either is provided.
-        if not (self.SECRET_KEY or self.SECRET_KEYS):
-            pass  # Neither is allowed in script usage.
-        elif self.SECRET_KEY and self.SECRET_KEYS:
-            raise ImproperlyConfigured('Only one of SECRET_KEY and SECRET_KEYS can be specified, not both.')
-        elif self.SECRET_KEY:
-            self.SECRET_KEYS = [self.SECRET_KEY]
-        else:
-            self.SECRET_KEY = self.SECRET_KEYS[0]
-
         if self.is_overridden('USE_DEPRECATED_PYTZ'):
             warnings.warn(USE_DEPRECATED_PYTZ_DEPRECATED_MSG, RemovedInDjango50Warning)
 
@@ -241,6 +236,8 @@ class Settings:
             warnings.warn(USE_L10N_DEPRECATED_MSG, RemovedInDjango50Warning)
 
     def is_overridden(self, setting):
+        if setting == 'SECRET_KEY':
+            setting = 'SECRET_KEYS'
         return setting in self._explicit_settings
 
     def __repr__(self):
@@ -249,6 +246,18 @@ class Settings:
             'settings_module': self.SETTINGS_MODULE,
         }
 
+    @property
+    def SECRET_KEY(self):
+        return self.SECRET_KEYS[0]
+
+    @SECRET_KEY.setter
+    def SECRET_KEY(self, value):
+        self.SECRET_KEYS = [value]
+
+    @SECRET_KEY.deleter
+    def SECRET_KEY(self):
+        del self.SECRET_KEYS
+
 
 class UserSettingsHolder:
     """Holder for user configured settings."""
@@ -289,6 +298,8 @@ class UserSettingsHolder:
         )
 
     def is_overridden(self, setting):
+        if setting == 'SECRET_KEY':
+            setting = 'SECRET_KEYS'
         deleted = (setting in self._deleted)
         set_locally = (setting in self.__dict__)
         set_on_default = getattr(self.default_settings, 'is_overridden', lambda s: False)(setting)
@@ -299,5 +310,20 @@ class UserSettingsHolder:
             'cls': self.__class__.__name__,
         }
 
+    @property
+    def SECRET_KEY(self):
+        try:
+            return self.SECRET_KEYS[0]
+        except TypeError:
+            return ''
+
+    @SECRET_KEY.setter
+    def SECRET_KEY(self, value):
+        self.SECRET_KEYS = [value]
+
+    @SECRET_KEY.deleter
+    def SECRET_KEY(self):
+        del self.SECRET_KEYS
+
 
 settings = LazySettings()
diff --git a/django/test/utils.py b/django/test/utils.py
index cb9672c91d..81005d4f8f 100644
--- a/django/test/utils.py
+++ b/django/test/utils.py
@@ -455,14 +455,6 @@ class override_settings(TestContextDecorator):
     enable_exception = None
 
     def __init__(self, **kwargs):
-        # Normalize SECRET_KEY(S)
-        has_secret_key = 'SECRET_KEY' in kwargs
-        has_secret_keys = 'SECRET_KEYS' in kwargs
-        if has_secret_key and not has_secret_keys:
-            kwargs['SECRET_KEYS'] = [kwargs['SECRET_KEY']] if kwargs['SECRET_KEY'] else []
-        if has_secret_keys and not has_secret_key:
-            kwargs['SECRET_KEY'] = kwargs['SECRET_KEYS'][0] if kwargs['SECRET_KEYS'] else None
-
         self.options = kwargs
         super().__init__()
 
diff --git a/tests/auth_tests/test_tokens.py b/tests/auth_tests/test_tokens.py
index 5f9ee69a75..cf39cb7b93 100644
--- a/tests/auth_tests/test_tokens.py
+++ b/tests/auth_tests/test_tokens.py
@@ -136,7 +136,7 @@ class TokenGeneratorTest(TestCase):
     @override_settings(SECRET_KEY='')
     def test_secret_lazy_validation(self):
         default_token_generator = PasswordResetTokenGenerator()
-        msg = 'The SECRET_KEYS setting must not be empty.'
+        msg = 'The elements of SECRET_KEYS must not be empty.'
         with self.assertRaisesMessage(ImproperlyConfigured, msg):
             default_token_generator.secrets
 
-- 
2.31.1


```

</details>

> The original way was trying to sync the two settings values, but I think the property comes out much cleaner.

Perhaps clearer and more robust in some ways. Not sure about cleaner given the need for the following in three places:

```diff
+        if setting == 'SECRET_KEY':
+            setting = 'SECRET_KEYS'
```

Are we sure we have nailed this in all the right places? Could this impact on third-party apps that do things with settings?

> (There's still the duplication with `UserSettingsHolder` which could be reduced.) Thoughts welcome!

The property stuff is nearly identical except for the catching of `TypeError`. It could be moved into a `SecretKeySettingCompatMixin` 😅 and then use a class variable to determine whether to suppress the exception...

I guess if it were possible to make the mixin more meaty, de-duplicating more of the stuff in `Settings` and `UserSettingsHolder`, the issue of the `if settings == SECRET_KEY:` duplication may also be reduced.

> …and then use a class variable to determine whether to suppress the exception...

That difference — catching the `TypeError`[0] —  is a point to review: I caught the exception in the one-place to get the tests to pass — but it may be that it rightly belongs in both. 🤔 

[0]: https://github.com/django/django/pull/13850/files#diff-b6f3108584c2db0b4c53253b6b3b5d5c60fbb3a82e7ed6544922fe689631fa43R326

Quick update: 

From a suggestion coming from discussion with @felixxm and @apollo13 — we're going to try a slightly different approach, keeping `SECRET_KEY` as the main value and adding a `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`, which would default to an empty list, to allow folks to do the rotation here. 

The `SECRET_KEYS` proposal is fine but 99% of folks would just have a single value, never rotate, and likely not get fully why the list was needed. (There's also a semantic point about the list head being significant.) 

Sticking with `SECRET_KEY` keeps that clearer. Adding the `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` should allow clearer messaging around _If you want to rotate_, and means we avoid this _mapping_ difficulty, that's proved, erm..., difficult. 

I'll sketch that out next.
That is a lot better than overloading/deprecating/replacing SECRET_KEY with SECRET_KEYS. And fully backwards compatible!
Thanks for your efforts on this pull! I'm curious if this still has a chance of making it into 4.0?

> Thanks for your efforts on this pull! I'm curious if this still has a chance of making it into 4.0?

Unfortunately no, the Django 4.0 feature freeze was on September 20, 2021.

@carltongibson I took a swing at implementing the fallback keys that you mentioned. The branch is at https://github.com/tim-schilling/django/tree/ticket-30360-fallback-keys. I did make an opinionated approach on supplying a new parameter, `read_keys` to `Signer`. It makes sense to me to identify the keys that can only be used for validation (perhaps I should have named it `validator_keys`). I also kept the same pattern regarding the setters and getters in `PasswordResetTokenGenerator`.
Hey @tim-schilling — super! Do you want to open a PR there? 🥇
Closing in favour of @tim-schilling's new PR. Thanks all for the input so far.
